actions.summary: Vote suggested labels of categories up or down (none takes the person's vote back) and suggest new labels in the person's name (each with their upvote, as the voting dialog's New suggestion does), and publish all of them together as one commit: the person's own file in the community annotation repository is written as published now plus these changes (a pull request when they cannot write to the repository), which others see on their next Pull. Put everything of a turn in one call: each call is one commit of the person's file and one question to them. Nothing else of the person's is published; votes that change nothing publish nothing. A label already suggested for its category is refused with its id (vote on it instead), and nothing of a call is published when any of it is refused. Asked of the person first; the history cannot take it back. Refused until the person has connected the repository and signed in to GitHub.

last_used.description: When it was last used (ISO 8601), or null.

saves.description: Bytes it spares the next opening, when known.

what.description: What it is, as the dialog says it.

name.description: Its file's name.

decoder_choices.description: Decoder choices measured in this browser.

my_datasets.description: The datasets opened in this browser (datasets_list lists each) and the files of this computer among them it can reopen.

room.description: What the browser says of the site's storage.

kept_when_space_is_low.description: Whether the browser keeps it when the disk runs low, when it says.

quota.description: Bytes the browser lets the site use, when it says.

usage.description: Bytes the site uses, when the browser says.

saved_states.description: The histories kept in this browser (history_saved_list lists each).

actions.summary: Everything kept in this browser for later visits, as the Stored dialog lists it: per dataset (its file's name and host) the converted copies, downloads, downloaded parts and gene indexes with their sizes; then the saved states, My datasets, the connection speeds and the decoder choices; and how much room the browser gives the site.

connection_speeds.description: The connection speeds remembered per host.

dataset.description: Every kept item of the dataset with this file name (stored_list).

decoder_choices.description: The decoder choices measured in this browser.

everything.description: Everything no open tab uses, as Remove all.

my_datasets.description: My datasets: the list and the handles of its files (my_datasets_forget forgets one).

saved_states.description: Every saved state of this browser (history_saved_delete deletes one).

connection_speeds.description: Hosts whose connection speed was forgotten.

held.description: Kept items that stay, in use by an open tab.

said.description: What the dialog says of it.

actions.summary: Remove what the Stored dialog removes: kept items by id, all a dataset's kept items, every saved state, My datasets (the list and the files' handles), the connection speeds, the decoder choices, or everything (Remove all). by.description: The categorical field to group the cells by.

key.description: The column name as the app shows it.

categories.description: Only these categories of `by` (else every category with cells); their arrows still lead into every category.

items.description: A category label as the legend shows it.

neighbors.description: How many nearest cells (in the embedding) each cell's arrow is shared among.

vector_field.description: The vector field, by name (dataset_summary lists them). Left out: the one the overlay shows, else the dataset's default, else the only one bound to the view's embedding; with several bound and none of those, name one.

view.description: The view whose embedding the arrows are read in: "View N"; the selected view when left out.

visible_only.description: Only the cells the view shows (its filters and hidden categories), as cells and as neighbors.

cells.description: Cells read (with a vector and a category).

empty.description: Categories left out for having no cells read.

coherence.description: How aligned its arrows are, 0 to 1: the length of the mean of their unit vectors (1: all point the same way; near 0: every way, or still).

direction.description: The mean direction as a unit vector in the embedding's axes (x, y[, z]).

heading.description: The direction in words on a 2-D view as drawn (right, up and right, …); null when not 2-D or not aligned (coherence below 0.2).

speed.description: Mean speed of its cells over the mean of all cells read (1: as fast as the average cell).

towards.description: Where its arrows lead, largest first: each category's share of the flow (own category included), shares of 2% or more.

without_vector.description: Cells left out for having no vector.

actions.summary: Where the cells of each category of a field are heading along a vector field (RNA velocity, a drift), in the embedding a view shows: per category, how fast (mean speed relative to the mean cell), how aligned its arrows are, their mean direction in the view's axes, and the categories its arrows lead into (each cell's arrow shared among its nearest cells by how directly it points at them, as scVelo's velocity graph does, here in the embedding). Read from the arrows as drawn in that embedding, not from the genes: an embedding can bend, merge or reverse a flow.
actions.title: Summarize where cells are heading

linked.description: true to link, false to unlink.

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

embedding.description: An embedding: the obsm array and the columns of it plotted.

columns.description: The 0-based columns plotted, one per dimension.

key.description: The obsm key, "X_umap".

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

actions.summary: Show one enabled embedding in a view; the view keeps it when the data mapping changes its defaults.

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

actions.summary: Select the view the sidebar edits and the camera controls drive.
actions.title: Select a view

branch.description: A branch of the tracker in use, by its name: the kept view shows what the selected view shows at its last step (coloring, filters, hidden cells, camera).

name.description: The kept view's name (view_rename gives or changes one later). A name for the view, one line of text ("Early", "Day 7, treated"): its row and its pane show it beside its number ("2 · Early"), a figure's panel after its letter ("B. Early": the figure letters its panels A, B, … in order, so a name needs no letter of its own). Not "View N".

actions.summary: Freeze the selected view as a panel of the multiview, with its coloring, filters and camera, and select it; with a branch, the view as it is at the last step of that branch of the history (to compare branches side by side).
actions.title: Keep the view

actions.summary: Show every view side by side (grid) or the selected view alone (single).
actions.title: Set the view layout

height.description: The height of the box the plot fits in, in pixels (source "export": of the box the figure is scaled into).

legend.description: Draw the color legend beside the plot (a figure picture; the screen has none).

source.description: figure: one view drawn as the figure export draws it (points, legend; no overlay), with plain settings (no title, 12 px text, the screen's background). screen: the view's pane as the screen shows it now, overlays included (the moving flow caught at this instant), no legend; the view must be on screen. export: the figure Export would download now, with every Figure export setting (figure_export_set), scaled down into width × height (ask 1200 × 1200 or more to read a multi-panel figure's titles).

view.description: The view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers it; the selected view when left out. Not with source "export" (it draws what Export would).

width.description: The width of the box the plot fits in, in pixels: the plot keeps the view's shape inside width × height, as the figure export frames it (the picture adds its margins and the legend). With source "export": the box the whole figure is scaled down into (never up).

label.description: The name the view was given (view_rename), or null.

notes.description: What the picture leaves out of what the view shows, or draws over it (a figure: an overlay it cannot draw; the screen: the legend; both: the highlighted cells drawn in the highlight's color over the coloring); for "export", first the figure's own size.

plot.description: The plot's size in the image: the largest rectangle of the view's shape inside the width × height asked for; null for an "export" picture of every view.

png.description: The image, base64-encoded PNG bytes (an agent receives it as an image).

view.description: The view drawn, by its name; null for an "export" picture of every view.

actions.summary: A PNG of a view as the figure export draws it (points, legend), or as the screen shows it now (source "screen": the vector field overlay, the connectivity edges and a playing camera path's caption included, which a figure cannot draw), or the whole figure exactly as Export would download it now with the Figure export settings (source "export": size, frame, background, fonts, title, panel titles, legends, every view while Export all views is on: check a figure with it before the person downloads it); returned as base64; nothing is downloaded.
actions.title: Take a picture of a view

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

actions.summary: Remove a view: a kept view is deleted; the live view (View 1) is hidden and every kept view stays. The last open view cannot be removed; view_clear shows the live view again.
actions.title: Remove a view

name.description: The new name, or null for none.

oneOf.description: A name for the view, one line of text ("Early", "Day 7, treated"): its row and its pane show it beside its number ("2 · Early"), a figure's panel after its letter ("B. Early": the figure letters its panels A, B, … in order, so a name needs no letter of its own). Not "View N".
No name: the view is known by its number alone.

view.description: A view: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers its rows (the live view is View 1 while it is shown, the kept views follow in the order they were kept).

actions.summary: Give a view a name of its own, or take it away (null): its row and its pane show it beside its number, a figure's panel title after the panel's letter ("B. Early"). The view is still named "View N" in actions.
actions.title: Name a view

active.description: The name of the view the controls act on ("View N").

reduced_motion.description: The person's system asks for reduced motion (an accessibility setting): a camera path goes to its last keyframe at once instead of playing, the camera stops when let go instead of gliding, a zoom arrives at once, the velocity flow is drawn as a still picture and highlights do not pulse. Say so when the person expects motion.

label.description: The name the view was given (view_rename), shown beside its number in its row, on its pane and as its panel's title in a figure; null when it has none.

live.description: The live view (the others are kept views).

name.description: What actions name the view by: "View N" as the Compare views list numbers it.

title.description: What its title chip shows (what it is colored by).

actions.summary: Each open view: its name (what actions name it by), the name it was given (view_rename), its title, the representation it shows, what it is colored by, its filters and camera; the layout; the highlight pages with their groups; whether the person's system asks for reduced motion.
actions.title: Read the views
